candidate.educational_objective: When standard patient-lift equipment cannot safely accommodate a dependent client, use appropriately selected assistive equipment and trained safe-patient-handling procedures rather than hazardous manual lifting.

options.A: Use the standard lift anyway if additional staff hold the client steady during the transfer.
options.B: Substitute a coordinated manual lift by several staff members so care is not delayed.
options.C: Obtain assistive lifting equipment appropriate for the client’s size and transfer needs and use trained staff according to the safe-patient-handling plan.
options.D: Avoid all repositioning and transfers until the client’s weight falls within the standard equipment limit.

candidate.rationale: NIOSH describes bariatric patients as including those whose weight exceeds the safety capacity of standard patient-lifting equipment, and current NIOSH/OSHA safe-patient-handling guidance emphasizes assistive lifting technology, appropriate device selection, staff training, and minimizing or eliminating manual lifting when possible. The safest response is therefore to obtain equipment that safely accommodates the client and use it with trained staff, rather than overload the standard device, default to manual lifting, or withhold necessary care.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Clients who exceed standard lifting-equipment safety capacity require safe-patient-handling planning with appropriate assistive lifting technology and trained staff; manual lifting should be minimized/eliminated when possible.
